# rlsbl transition

The lifecycle-and-license record, .strictmetadata/lifecycle-and-license/lifecycle-and-license.toml: each releasable's dated lifecycle (active, non-releasing, retired; without a period in effect, active once released and unreleased before), license, and identity periods, the registry names it holds, the tags that release no version: license and lifecycle facts only (confidential terms live in the confidential-term list, which a release scans for). A repository is confidential while a releasable's license is proprietary. A command that opens a period closes the subject's period in effect on today's date first. A command that changes the record validates the whole record against the declarations, writes it, and commits it with the Autogenerated trailer, together with whatever else its own help says it changes.

## transition show

Print the lifecycle-and-license record and every rule's verdict on today's date: whether the repository's GitHub visibility agrees with its licenses (GitHub is asked; a visibility that cannot be had is unknown, with the reason), which releasables are refused public outputs, what a confidential or private repository does not publish, which releasables a lifecycle keeps from releasing, the proprietary periods a declassification squashes, the closed identities owning tags, and whether the record keeps every registry name and closed period the record HEAD commits holds. Problems that make the record invalid against the declarations are listed. Works in a repository without declarations or without a record.

**Effect:** read_only

## transition lifecycle

Close a releasable's or member's lifecycle period on today's date and open one with --status: active, non-releasing (its releases are refused), or retired (its release history is a record). A releasable without a lifecycle period in effect has a derived status, never recorded: active when its release archives record a release, and unreleased when they do not, which refuses its releases. Recording active for an unreleased releasable is the owner's decision that allows its first release. The subject is declared, or one the record already holds a lifecycle period of. A status its lifecycle period in effect already holds is refused. Retiring a declared releasable of a workspace is one commit: besides the period, the releasable and every member versioned under it leave releasables.toml, their open identities close (so the tags they owned are accounted for), their release hook directories under .strictmetadata/release-hooks/ and the releasable's changelog validation cache are deleted through saferm, the scaffold state stops managing the members' files, and the routers and the root CHANGELOG.md are regenerated without them; the releasable's changelog and release directories stay where they are, as its closed history. --subject repeats with --status retired only, each one a declared releasable: they retire together in that one commit, the routers regenerated once without all of them, which retires releasables that block each other's retirement (each one's publish workflow gone with its directory, so the routers cannot be regenerated while another is still declared). Refused before anything is written: the releasable of a standalone repository (the whole repository is archived instead), a releasable holding the root member, a member that stays depending on one that leaves, an options entry scoped to a leaving member, a release in progress, and an uncommitted change to a path the retirement writes.

**Effect:** mutating · **consequential** (prompts before running; `--approve-consequential` skips)

### Flags

| Name | Short | Type | Presence | Env | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--subject` |  | list[str] (unique) | required |  | The releasable or member whose lifecycle changes; repeatable with --status retired only, once per declared releasable retired in the same commit |
| `--status` |  | str | required |  | The status from today Values: `active` (released as usual; for an unreleased releasable, its first release is allowed), `non-releasing` (its releases are refused until it is active again), `retired` (its release history is closed, a record nothing releases from; a declared releasable leaves the declarations). |
| `--reason` |  | str | required |  | Why, in the operator's own words; the record keeps it |

## transition license

Close a releasable's license period on today's date and open one under --license, an SPDX identifier. proprietary is refused (`transition classify` makes a releasable proprietary), and so is a change that would leave no releasable proprietary (`transition declassify` takes the repository public, squashing its proprietary history first). A license the releasable already has is refused.

**Effect:** mutating · **consequential** (prompts before running; `--approve-consequential` skips)

## transition identity

Record an identity period of a subject: its releasable name, package name, project name, Go module path, tag format, or repository URL (--facet), with --value, the registry it is a name in (--registry; none for an identity that is not a registry name; a package name is a name in one registry, so its identity names one and is kept per registry), and the tag namespace it owned (--tag-pattern, repeatable, globs where * matches any run of characters). Without --from the identity starts today and the subject's open identity of the facet (in the same registry, for a package name) closes today; with --from (and --until for a closed one) it is recorded as given, a dead identity's included, whose tags are then accounted for instead of reported.

**Effect:** mutating · **consequential** (prompts before running; `--approve-consequential` skips)

### Flags

| Name | Short | Type | Presence | Env | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--subject` |  | str | required |  | The releasable or member the identity belonged to |
| `--facet` |  | str | required |  | Which identity it is Values: `releasable-name` (the releasable's name), `package-name` (a published package's name), `project-name` (the project's name), `go-module-path` (a Go module path), `tag-format` (the tag format), `repository-url` (the repository's URL). |
| `--value` |  | str | required |  | The identity's value: the name, path, format, or URL |
| `--registry` |  | str | optional |  | The registry the value is a name in; omitted for an identity that is not a registry name Values: `npm` (the npm registry), `pypi` (the Python Package Index), `go` (the Go module proxy). |
| `--tag-pattern` |  | list[str] (unique) | optional |  | A glob of the tags the identity owned while its period ran; repeatable |
| `--from` |  | str | optional |  | The identity's first day (YYYY-MM-DD); omitted, it starts today and closes the open identity of the facet |
| `--until` |  | str | optional |  | The first day after a closed identity (YYYY-MM-DD) |
| `--reason` |  | str | required |  | Why, in the operator's own words; the record keeps it |

| `until-needs-from` | `--until` requires `--from`. |

## transition unversioned-tag

Record a tag that releases no version (a nightly marker, an imported vendor tag), so release backfill, release reconcile, and the tag checks account for it instead of reporting it. A tag the record holds already is refused.

**Effect:** mutating · **consequential** (prompts before running; `--approve-consequential` skips)

## transition classify

Make a releasable proprietary: open a proprietary license period for it on today's date, which makes the repository confidential and from then on refuses every public output of the releasable (registry packages and writes, build attestations, public docs, blog posts). GitHub must already report the repository private; making it private is the owner's action outside rlsbl, and a public repository is refused naming it. Run the quiet deprecate and yank of anything it published before classifying it: afterwards no registry write is made for it.

**Effect:** mutating · **consequential** (prompts before running; `--approve-consequential` skips)

| `--reason` |  | str | required |  | Why, in the operator's own words; the record keeps it |

## transition declassify

Take a confidential repository public. --license names, for every releasable whose license is proprietary and no other, the public license it takes. In order: each proprietary period's commits on the release branch's first-parent history (by committer date) are squashed through `safegit scrub squash` into one commit carrying a fixed message that names no confidential term, keeping the public history before and after it (a period whose commits are not contiguous, or that holds a merge commit, is refused before anything is rewritten, naming the commit); the changelog's commit ids and the archives' release commits are repaired through the rewrite, and a release whose commit was folded into a commit carrying another tree is recorded unrecoverable; the proprietary licenses close today and the --license ones open; a history-rewrite archive records the run; all of it is committed; the branch and every moved tag are force-pushed with leases taken before the first squash; each moved tag's GitHub Release is rewritten from the record; and the GitHub repository is made public. The closing report lists the commits of the proprietary periods origin held before the first squash, which GitHub keeps serving by their ids after the force-push and only GitHub support can purge (the owner asks for it at the declassification); a ref origin holds at a commit this repository lacks is refused before anything is rewritten, naming the fetch. A run that stops is finished by running the same command again, from the step that stopped it (.strictmetadata/.release-state/declassify-result.json). Refused while a release or a scrub is in progress, off a release branch, without an origin remote, and when --reason carries a term of the confidential-term list. Requires safegit 0.31.1 or newer. --dry-run prints the squashes and writes nothing.

**Effect:** mutating · **consequential** (prompts before running; `--approve-consequential` skips)

| `--reason` |  | str | required |  | Why the repository goes public; the record, the rewrite's archive, and the commit carry it |

## transition init-minimal-record

Write the minimal lifecycle-and-license record (its format version alone, with the manifest naming strictspec) into a repository rlsbl does not manage, and commit both with the Autogenerated trailer. With no license period the repository is public, so what it publishes is scanned for confidential terms. A repository holding release declarations or an old-layout directory is rlsbl's, and is refused; so is one that already holds a record.

**Effect:** mutating
